summary: This is a Room domain class: a blueprint for one room in a house, holding its name, length, and width, with methods to read and change those values and to print the object in readable form.

lines.text: Lengths and widths are declared as double because room dimensions are measured, not counted, so 12.5 feet needs to be representable.
This empty no-argument constructor is the piece that differs from House: it lets you create a bare Room first and fill in the details later through the setters.

lines.text: Two constructors with different parameter lists can coexist in one class; Java picks the one that matches the arguments you supply.
The parameter and the field share the name name, so this.name says "the field belonging to this object" while the bare name is the value passed in.
Keeping the fields private and exposing setters is what lets the class stay in charge of its own data, which is the whole point of encapsulation.
The escape sequence '\'' puts a literal single quote into the text, so a room's name appears in quotes when the object is printed.
